summary: I is an ordinary intransitive cooking predicate; II introduces the cook and an object; II Detransitive suppresses that cook. JTM 2.11/3 and 2.5/11 show this contrast within one verse. No agentive or experiencer coding is evidenced.

The qaṭəl base bašəl and feminine bašilo contrast with Infectum bošəl/bəšlo. Part act. masculine bašilo and plural bašile overlap in meaning with the finite results, so classification follows form and agreement where available. I Preterit Intransitive and provisional Infectum-wa receive example boxes without new lexical senses.

Cooking on a baking iron, grilling meat and cooking bread remain within inherited II.1; German backen/braten does not establish a Turoyo distinction. Human undergoers in JTM 4.2/9 and MAC NE Habirman Xatun/5 are participant extensions of I.1.

The II Detransitive Infinitiv section already mixes the process noun bišolo and product noun bəššolo. New cooking-time and negative 'without cooking' examples retain that inherited filing; the label does not imply a finite Detransitive construction.

The curse bašəl babawo in 96/364 is not used as a plain culinary Preterit example. The one supplied token cannot settle a frozen optative or adjectival analysis; confirmation is requested rather than publishing an invented idiom.
All three Jan occurrences support the established cooking system: II with a cook and patient, I with food as a state-bearing subject. No new sense, idiom or form box is required after round 1.

Reader thin_cell flags refer to the unrevised entry. II Infectum-wa and II Preterit sense 1 each have five examples after round 1; I Part act. has four. The new meat/cooked adjective does not overturn that earlier classification.

The exact form mbašlənne at Jan 2.4/964 is compatible with the active Infectum/object pattern already seen in round 1. Its past setting alone cannot prove Preterit; keep the token as morphological research evidence rather than add a doubtful example.
Jan Beṯ-Şawoce English is the supplied project machine translation, not an edition translation. Analyses rest on the Turoyo; any English quoted below is copied from that supplied translation.
Confirm JTM 2.5/8 bəšliwo as Infectum bəšli plus -wo, rather than reduced Preterit-wa. Its new Infectum-wa box is provisional; no new stem or sense depends on it.

Resolve finite feminine bašilo versus masculine Part act. bašilo with stress and agreement, especially JTM 1.1/84, JTM 2.9/3 and MAC NE Habirman Xatun/5; plural bašili versus bašile likewise needs recording confirmation.
JL 18.6/12 leaves w bəṯr me d bašəl untranslated. No example is quoted for that token; recover the matching German before adding it.
Confirm object/agent segmentation of mbašlulle and mbašlowalle and singular soməq after the plural flapjacks in JTM 2.1/3. Do not regularize their spelling.
JTM 2.4/4 bəšolo may be an event noun, product noun or reduced adjective. It is withheld as a new Infinitiv example pending clarification.

Check source omissions in 4/49, Bašele versus inherited bašel-a at 36/114, and mbašela versus inherited mbašéla-le at 65/291. The supplied variants do not establish which edition text should be corrected.
Is 96/364 u bašəl babawo a fixed curse? A glossary search for bašəl found no idiom; its grammatical form and headword remain unresolved.
Confirm the contracted second-person endings of mbašalxu and mbašeluxlan in the ember episode; the damaging-heating interpretation is clear from the overt patients and fire context.
Confirm mbašlənne at Jan 2.4/964, especially whether -nne indexes a patient or the l-agent series. It is provisionally Infectum and withheld from publication as form evidence.
English typo: meet → meat
rationale: The food noun is meat; meet is a verb. The Turoyo phrase explicitly has baṣro.

summary: German typo: Früstück → Frühstück
rationale: The German noun is Frühstück; the supplied translation of 65/291 also has Frühstück.

summary: Missing accusative ending: ein Löffel → einen Löffel
rationale: Löffel is the masculine accusative object of kochte. The supplied edition has einen Löffel Linsensuppe.

summary: German typo: Küchen → Küche
rationale: The singular noun required by einer is Küche. The supplied edition reads in einer kleinen Küche gekocht.
